abstract: Let $u$ be a vertex of a strongly regular graph $\mathrm{srg}(45,22,10,11)$, with local graph $X$ on the 22 neighbours of $u$. A $(5,5)$-good such graph, with no $K_5$ and no independent 5-set, would show $R(5,5)=46$. The adjacency block $M$ between $N(u)$ and the 22 non-neighbours is a 0/1 factor of $F(X)=11I+10J-X-X^2$, and the graph on the non-neighbours must complete it. When $F$ is nonsingular the completion is forced and is an explicit test. Singular $F$ is common among known graphs: 22,174 of the 103,500 rooted graphs from Spence's two-graphs on 46 points have $F$ of corank 2, 4 or 6. We treat the completion step at singular roots. For a fixed factor, the completions are exactly $C+T$ with $C=M^\top F^+XM$ and $T$ a symmetric matrix on $\ker M$ satisfying $T^2+T=11P_{\ker M}$, a diagonal condition and a 0/1 condition; this makes completion a finite exact procedure at every corank. At corank 2 a factor has at most two completions. Two occur exactly when $\ker M$ is spanned by balanced $\pm1$ vectors on two disjoint 6-sets with a fixed cross pattern, and the completions differ by complementing the 36 pairs between them, an instance of Wang-Qiu-Hu switching. In a $(5,5)$-good graph this configuration contains a $K_5$, so a $(5,5)$-good completion at a corank-2 root is the only srg completion of its labelled factor. At any corank, two completions differ by a matrix whose column space is an invariant subspace of $\ker M$ of even dimension, and a rank-2 difference is again this switching, so a $(5,5)$-good completion has no rank-2 alternative. All results are proved by hand; computations on known graphs are controls only. Whether a singular local graph of a $(5,5)$-good graph exists, and uniqueness for differences of rank at least 4, remain open.

change_summary:
Scoped correction approved by the supervisor after the v1 review. No theorem, proof or evidence changes.
1. Attribution (review of v1): the switch of Proposition 3.2 is an instance of Ihringer-Simoens [8, Sec. 4.1.2, Thm 7] in every case, with t = 1, C11 = S1+, C21 = S1-. The Remark after Proposition 3.2 now gives this direct comparison: the invariant-vector equation gives the constant degree difference of condition (ii); vertices of S2 meet exactly one whole class (case (iii)(a) or (b)); all other vertices meet both equally (case (iii)(c)); the swap complements exactly S1 x S2. The two 'not checked' qualifications are removed (Section 1 item 2, 'What is not new', the Remark). The abstract now says 'an instance of Wang-Qiu-Hu switching' in place of 'a Wang-Qiu-Hu switching when one side is regular'. [7, Thm 2] is still cited for the case where one side is regular.
2. Portability (review of v1): code/singular_controls.py takes nauty's labelg path as --labelg PATH (default: labelg on PATH) instead of a hard-coded path; README.md records the Python, numpy, sympy and nauty versions. No output was regenerated.
The contribution is unchanged: the exhaustive fixed-factor classification and its Ramsey exclusion.
title: Completion of singular local factors of an srg(45,22,10,11)
